name: Hitachi Energy India Ltd
title: Hitachi Energy India Ltd - 543187 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Hitachi Energy India Q4 FY26 revenue rose 46.2% YoY to Rs 2,754.1 Cr, with record order backlog of Rs 29,555 Cr at FY26 end.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 orders were Rs 2,422.5 Cr (up 10.6% YoY) and revenue was Rs 2,754.1 Cr (up 46.2% YoY), with PAT of Rs 330.5 Cr. For FY26, revenue reached Rs 8,147.7 Cr (up 27.6%) and PAT Rs 987.8 Cr (up 157.3%), while FY26 orders were broadly flat at Rs 18,456.5 Cr (up 1.6%). Management highlighted completion of the 1,000 MW Mumbai City infeed HVDC project and a new Rs 2,000 Cr capex approval, taking cumulative capex to nearly Rs 4,000 Cr. Analyst questions focused on weak non-HVDC domestic orders, export mix, margins, and royalty.

segments.name: HVDC
segments.commentary: HVDC revenue in FY26 was about Rs 1,100 Cr, roughly 15% of Rs 8,000 Cr total revenue, per CEO and CFO; management says it is margin-accretive but not yet substantial. The 1,000 MW Mumbai City infeed (VSC) project was commissioned in FY26.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Export revenue was about 25% of FY26 revenue and export orders are in a similar range, though lower in Q4 due to large domestic orders; management cites a 25-30% average, with a 3-pronged model (allocated markets, global feeder factory products like 66 kV breakers and COMBIFLEX relays, and component contract manufacturing).

segments.name: Services
segments.commentary: Q4 services orders were high, driven by a control and protection upgrade for MSETCL in India. Management named strengthening India services as a key pillar.

segments.name: Transmission / Transformers
segments.commentary: Transmission order intake showed a small dip in FY26 due to mismatch in large order values versus FY25. Management says the transformer pipeline is very strong and the temporary slowdown is behind them.

segments.name: Data centers, renewables, industry
segments.commentary: Order intake grew across industry, data centers, railways and renewables in FY26. Management says data centers are under 2 GW in India today, with a projected 6-9x expansion; Hitachi targets about 15% of data center capex as addressable.

guidance_outlook: Management declined to give forward-looking numbers; CEO said 'we don't give any forward-looking numbers going forward' when asked about FY27 domestic non-HVDC order inflow.
Pipeline described qualitatively as very strong across renewables, data centers, transmission and transformers, excluding HVDC; industries described as intermittent but recovering.

HVDC: management said there is no capacity limitation to take more HVDC projects in the coming year or year after; at least 3, if not 4, HVDC projects expected in the pipeline over the next 2 years, with both LCC and VSC.

New greenfield large power transformer plant at Karjan, Vadodara: groundbreaking on 12 June; capacity baseline 30 GVA, up to 40 GVA depending on product mix; completion targeted by last quarter of CY2028.
Oct 2024 capex programme projects are under way and take 3 to 4 years to complete.

Data centers: India data center capacity under 2 GW, with projections of 13-18 GW; management cited 6-9x expansion. Hitachi treats each data center as 15% of addressable capex; management declined to give an absolute Hitachi figure.
Export share guided as a ballpark of about 25-30% on average, excluding large lump orders such as HVDC; management declined to give exact numbers.
Price pass-through: most of the portfolio has commodity price variation clauses; freight costs linked to Hormuz-related disruption are not passable and are being managed.
Management said the transformer pipeline is very strong and the transmission slowdown is behind them; transformer delivery lead times cited as 12-15 months depending on the product.
capex_capacity: Board approved additional Rs 2,000 Cr capex in Q4 FY26, over and above the Oct 2024 programme; cumulative capex close to Rs 4,000 Cr.

New greenfield large power transformer facility at Karjan, Vadodara, Gujarat, to make LPTs and HVDC converter transformers, targeted for completion by Q4 CY2028; capacity baseline 30 GVA, up to 40 GVA by product mix.
Oct 2024 capex programme projects are under way and take 3-4 years to complete, per management.
Bangalore factory adding 7th and 8th lines for power quality products, on top of 6 existing lines.
Management said the capacity addition is demand-driven and not aimed at local content requirements or product gaps.
demand_pricing: Order backlog Rs 29,555.3 Cr at 31 Mar 2026, up 53.6% YoY; management cited multi-quarter revenue visibility.
Domestic non-HVDC orders: an analyst said they fell in FY26 versus FY25; management said investigation showed no decline and that growth occurred in domestic business.
Price pass-through: most of the portfolio has commodity price variation clauses; freight and Middle East related costs (Hormuz) are not passable and are being managed.
Royalty: management said new technologies and products (e.g., data centers, energy storage) are sourced from the parent and royalty is paid to access them; R&D is managed centrally at the parent.
Local content: management said it exceeds the recent government local content requirements.

qa_highlights.question: How are export orders generated, and do you compete with parent entities?
qa_highlights.answer: Management described a 3-pronged model: allocated markets developed long-term with local sales offices, global feeder factory products (66 kV breakers, COMBIFLEX relays) sold directly or via Hitachi offices, and component manufacturing for other Hitachi factories. Management said no two Hitachi companies compete in the same market.

qa_highlights.question: Why are HVDC margins below peers and what is the HVDC share of revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: HVDC revenue was about Rs 1,100 Cr, roughly 15% of FY26 revenue of Rs 8,000 Cr; HVDC is margin-accretive but not large yet. Services, exports and base business are the focus.

qa_highlights.question: What drove the sequential gross margin decline in Q4?
qa_highlights.answer: CFO attributed the sequential contraction to product mix. Gross margin for FY26 improved about 200 bps to 40% from about 38% in FY25.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for non-HVDC domestic orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said non-HVDC domestic orders had not declined on investigation. It noted some capacity is being absorbed by the HVDC portfolio. Management did not give forward numbers and said the pipeline is strong across renewables, data centers and transmission.

qa_highlights.question: What is the new capex capacity and its phasing?
qa_highlights.answer: The new Karjan plant adds 30 GVA baseline (up to 40 GVA). Management called demand multi-year and said the plant completes by Q4 CY2028; groundbreaking is on 12 June.

qa_highlights.question: What is the data center opportunity for Hitachi over five years?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said India data center capacity is under 2 GW versus projections of 13-18 GW. Hitachi targets about 15% of each data center's capex as addressable, and did not give an absolute Hitachi figure.

risks_watch: Gross margin volatility from product mix; Q4 sequential decline cited by an analyst.
Commodity inflation, elevated freight and Middle East-related supply chain pressure, with non-passable freight costs.
Royalty payments to the parent rising as new technology is sourced; other expenses at 16.9% of revenue in FY26.
Non-HVDC domestic order intake: management disputed an analyst's view of a decline, but the FY26 backlog growth is HVDC-led.
Execution on the Karjan plant and the Oct 2024 capex programme (3-4 year timelines).
Unrealised exchange loss of Rs 31.5 Cr in Q4 FY26.
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on demand and backlog, with a multi-year growth narrative and approval of new capex. Evasive on specific numbers: management declined to give forward guidance, exact export share, Hitachi's share of data center capex, and HVDC margin detail.
key_quotes: A key highlight is our record order backlog of Rs 29,555 crores as of March 31, 2026, which provides a strong revenue visibility for several quarters going forward.

This is an accelerated execution program, and we would like to complete this state-of-the-art Greenfield transformer factory to produce our large power transformers and HVDC converter transformer by last quarter of 2028 calendar year.
It's not a 1- or 2-year, 3-year story we are talking about a multiyear growth story.

growth.why: Management declined to give forward numbers, but record backlog of Rs 29,555 Cr (+53.6% YoY) gives multi-quarter visibility, HVDC has no capacity constraint with 3-4 projects expected over two years, and the Karjan LPT plant (30-40 GVA) targets completion by Q4 CY2028, so FY27 growth is supported mainly by the existing order book.
